recipes.name: Caramel Apple Crumble Pie
ingredients_raw: 6 apples - peeled, cored, and thinly sliced

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine oats, 1/2 cup brown sugar, slivered almonds, 1/4 cup flour, and 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon; cut in butter using 2 knives or pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Set aside.
Roll pie dough into a circle to fit a 9-inch pie plate; place crust in the pie plate. Trim crust, crimping edges.

Toss apples and lemon juice together in a bowl to prevent browning. Combine 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1 tablespoon flour, and 2 teaspoons cinnamon in a separate bowl; toss with apples to coat. Drizzle 1/4 cup caramel sauce over bottom of pie crust; add apple mixture. Drizzle with remaining 1/4 cup caramel sauce. Sprinkle crumble topping evenly over apples.
Bake in the preheated oven until apples are tender and crust is brown, 50 to 60 minutes,

raw_recipe.headline: Caramel Apple Crumble Pie
raw_recipe.description: In this recipe, the combination of caramel apple pie and apple crumble is sublime. The pie is sweet with its pastry crust and cinnamon-spiced oat topping.

review.reviewBody: This is actually my recipe and I have to say that they altered it a little when they published it. I actually sprinkle a tablespoon or two of flour into the bottom of the crust to prevent the sogginess from the juices. It works really well.

I did use granny smith but left out the lemon juice and it was good this way. I just forgot it, but since an ealreir review said granny smiths were bitter, I think it was a good thing. I also skipped the almonds in the topping because I didn't have any, and it was great. The second time I made it, I made it in a 9x13 aluminum pan and did 1 1/2 times the recipe and I used pecans because it is what I already had. I drizzed it with a little of the carmel sauce for looks too. I used the No roll Pie Crust I from this site and it was great too. Mixed the dough right in the pan I spread it in. Very easy. Great recipe. taking it to a wienie roast tonight. Oh, I did double the cinnamon in the topping, but I love cinnamon.

This pie gets rave reviews from everyone I bake it for. There are only 2 things I would change: 1. Melt the butter, don't cube it for the topping. Otherwise you end up with butter clumps and dry flour patches on top. Also, wait until after the pie bakes to add Carmel on top. The type I used hardened when I baked it and made the pie chewy on top. Otherwise, it's great!
Was a hit a Christmas dinner adding 2Tableapoons of flour to crust before Carmel saved pie crust

This turned out fabulous! I doubled the recipe and made two pies, and they were delicious. Gave the other between family and friends. I took a lot of the reviews and added flour to the bottom of the pie and 1 tsp cornstarch to thicken it up. I wasn't runny at all! I also omitted the caramel during the baking process, since everyone said you couldn't taste it. I added the caramel on each piece before serving, and you still couldn't really taste it over all the other flavors, but with vanilla ice cream it was great. I took a tip off the pie shell box and after baking for 15 minutes, I put foil around the crust's edges, and they baked perfect! Will be making this again next year.

This recipe is good for a base but I made quite a few changes after reading the reviews first. I followed the suggestion to add a little more flour so I used 2 tablespoons flour. I made homemade caramel sauce and put some in the bottom and on top of the apples as well as drizzled over the finished pie. I didin't think 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon was quite enough for crumble topping so I added a whole teaspoon. I cut back on the brown sugar in the pie filling to 1/4 cup since the caramel and the crumb topping was already sweet. I want to taste a littel tartness from the apples. Suggestions for soggy crust. When you are preheating your oven, pop your crust in for about 5 minutes before you fill. Someone suggested to me a long time ago and I do every pie this way, even the ones I freeze. I have no problems with doughy or soggy crust. I'm giving a 4 star since it is a good start to a pie but I did have to altar the recipe.

I make this pie EVERY Thanksgiving, Christmas, and if not Christmas, then for New Years!! I also bake the pies (I double the recipe and make two pies) for 2.5-3 hours til the apples are soft. It is my families favorite pie and is requested every year!! I add a little extra flour to the apple mixture and for less juice you can add a tablespoon of corn starch to the apple seasoning mixture to thicken the juice. Sometimes think outside the box and don’t bash the recipe. There is usually a fix of some sort and you may have to play with it til you get the results you desire.

I made this recipe, the juice from the apple mixture ruined the pie crust, it turned into a cobbler. Tasty, but a mess to serve. Next time if I try this recipe again, I would add corn starch or tapioca to the apple mixture to solidify the pie filling, and I would cut the caramel in half, and not put any caramel on the bottom pie crust, only on top of the mixture. Interestingly, I read many reviews that stated they would add more cinnamon, I would do the opposite, I tasted too much cinnamon.

Made this for thanksgiving. It got rave reviews from everyone! I will agree with others that I couldn’t taste the caramel as much as I’d like, but it was so yummy no one minded. I might try a higher quality caramel sauce next time. My only real complaint was the crust. I followed some of the tips in the reviews and put a tablespoon of flour on the crust before adding the ingredients, added a couple teaspoons of cornstarch to the apple mixture, and even baked the crust for 5 minutes like one review suggested and the crust still was basically raw. I’m not an avid pie maker so I’m not sure what I did wrong. I will definitely make it again but maybe I will try pre-baking the crust or just making it without the crust as a crisp.

BEST apple pie recipe ever! The only change I made was to use both Honeycrisp and Granny Smith apples.
 My crust turned out fine but I would recommend a dip dish pie plate as the topping can be too much for the smaller ones.
 My family LOVED it, and it has now replaced my pumpkin cheesecake as the most-requested holiday dessert. (Fine by me, as it's a lot easier to make this one!)
i made this and had an outstanding results i also added one or two table spoons of corn flour to the filling and it soaks up most of the juices

Fantastic pie! Everyone loved it. I loved how easy it was to make. I think I would add pecans instead of slivered almonds-or in addition to. I think it takes the longer time to bake. Excellent with vanilla ice cream.
I used walnuts instead of pecans.
awesome recipe. made it many times
I could make this every week it was so good, but I need a better pastry crust.
Fabulous as good as it sounds!
The rating is based on the topping alone. I came out with a spreadable paste.
Yes and after reading reviews I made a great one! Yum! Thanks!

This was delicious.. My first apple pie! I drizzled caramel sauce on top of the crumb coating and it formed a delectable candy texture. I tried both the corn starch and flour on the bottom so did not really think it came out soggy. Next time I would omit the caramel sauce on the bottom because some find it too sweet!
I love the crumble on top! I made it just as the recipe called for. I think next time I'll try the flour/cornstarch.
